summary: Round 5, tests only. Measured in a copy of the staged bytes (376 sequencer tests, baseline green). Last-pair-only mutation of the order loop (for (int r = Math.max(1, inSegmentOrder.size() - 1); ...)) is KILLED, by exactly one fixture: aStreamOutOfOrderOnlyInANEARLYPairIsStillCaught. The mirror mutation (first-pair-only, r < Math.min(2, size())) is killed by exactly one fixture too: aStreamOutOfOrderOnlyInALATERPairIsStillCaught -- so the new fixture neither subsumes nor is subsumed by its twin. Dropping the break still dies only on aStreamOutOfOrderTWICEIsStillONEViolation, and < to <= still dies only on TWOSegmentsStartingAtTheSAMEOffsetIsI2Alone, so no existing fixture lost its unique kill. The clean delta(1, 3, 0) at sequence 1 in both new fixtures introduces no spurious gap or I2: baseline is green with containsExactly("order"), and deleting the offset-order sort makes both fixtures fail with the extra names, which proves the exact-list assertion can see one. The known minor stands: the sequence constant has MOVED to 2L, measured surviving the whole suite; 1L is killed by the LATER fixture. Agreeing it becomes a backlog row rather than a sixth round.

findings.title: the new fixture's javadoc says the records cover 3..9; they cover 3..8, as its own assertion description says
findings.failure_scenario: Runs are B 2 records at 3 (3..4), A 2 at 5 (5..6), C 2 at 7 (7..8) -- coverage is 3..8. The javadoc reads 'the records cover 3..9 exactly once' while the assertion five lines below reads '3..8 covered exactly once'. Nothing in the assertion is wrong and no mutation survives because of it, so this changes no result. It matters only because a reader checking whether the fixture is contiguous -- which is the whole reason no gap or I2 fires -- gets two answers from one fixture, and 3..9 would need a seventh record. Recommend the commit body or a backlog row, NOT a sixth round: fixing it adds prose that is the next round's surface.
findings.surviving_mutation: none -- this is a comment, not an assertion; stated as minor and explicitly not blocking.

findings.title: carried forward from round 4: the sequence-constant mutation moved to 2L rather than dying
findings.failure_scenario: Replacing e.sequence() in the order violation's message with the literal 2L leaves all 376 sequencer tests green (measured). Both fixtures that assert the detail string now place the permuted delta at sequence 2, so one fixture asserting one string still cannot separate the field from the literal equal to it -- 1L is now killed, by aStreamOutOfOrderOnlyInALATERPairIsStillCaught, but 2L is not. Consequence if the field were really a constant: a failing simulation seed reporting 'the delta at sequence 2' for a permutation at any other sequence, which is the string this fixture's own comment says is how a pinned seed gets debugged. Killing it needs the sequence asserted in a SECOND fixture at a different sequence. I agree with filing it as a backlog row rather than fixing it here.
findings.surviving_mutation: + 2L in place of + e.sequence() in the "runs out of order within the delta at sequence " message (Invariants.java:193). Whole sequencer suite green.
